reference_summary: A downed conductor on the Synthetic Meridian Loop feeder left the entire branch de-energized for nineteen minutes before crews arrived. The Synthetic Meridian Loop relay group retained a ground overcurrent pickup of 240 primary amperes from the prior seasonal configuration. Restoration switching closed the loop backfeed path while the legacy pickup threshold remained active on the relay group. Backfeed inrush from the Synthetic Meridian Loop warehouse transformer bank exceeded the legacy pickup within two cycles of the closing operation. The relay group tripped the loop breaker, and the restoration attempt failed before any customer load was picked up. Synthetic Meridian Loop operators re-energized the feeder from the alternate source after manually blocking the ground element.
title: Protection-Setting Mismatch During Feeder Restoration on Synthetic Meridian Loop

reference_summary: Synthetic Ridgeline plant recorded a measured bus voltage sag to 71 percent for 420 milliseconds on the independent channel. Controller indicated 74 percent sag while the independent channel showed 71 percent, creating a three point discrepancy. The primary cause was a phase-to-ground arc at Synthetic Ridgeline transformer bank initiating the voltage depression. A contributing condition was elevated ambient temperature raising winding resistance above the nominal threshold. Inverter DC bus current rose from 12 to 19 amperes as the converter compensated for the AC voltage depression. Synthetic Ridgeline load bus experienced a 28 kilowatt power deficit lasting 420 milliseconds during the voltage depression. The corrective action was resetting the Synthetic Ridgeline capacitor bank and verifying its reactive draw to rated values.

The corrective action was to widen the synthetic undervoltage threshold from 0.71 to 0.58 per unit.

reference_summary: At 14:03:12 the Synthetic Ridgeway hub issued a reserve activation command, and the field relay acknowledged receipt 0.4 seconds later. The independent audit channel, Synthetic Kestrel, recorded the same command 0.3 seconds after issuance, confirming the order left the hub promptly. Operators had scheduled a firmware refresh for the telemetry buffer at 13:40, but the refresh stalled when a checksum comparison returned mismatched values. Because the indicated voltage sat below the 13.9 kilovolt threshold, the hub withheld the activation signal for 47 seconds. Reserve delivery finally began 47 seconds after the command, and the 12 megawatt obligation was met 51 seconds late. The corrective action was to add a timestamp-freshness gate that rejects any sample older than 60 seconds before it reaches the hub.
title: Reserve Activation Delay Traced to Stale Telemetry Buffer at Synthetic Ridgeway Control Hub

reference_summary: At 14:03:12 the Synthetic Meridian Control Desk observed feeder loading cross the armed trip boundary on channel Alpha-7. Operators at Synthetic Meridian noted the first threshold excursion during a routine switching sequence, not an unplanned disturbance. The root fault was a stale coordination table: the under-frequency relay pairing had not been refreshed after the prior network reconfiguration. A contributing condition was that two adjacent feeders shared a single measurement transformer, blurring per-feeder current estimates. When the stale pairing engaged, the upstream breaker opened before the downstream relay had finished its timing window. Approximately 1,240 synthetic customers lost service for 47 minutes before restoration completed. The corrective action was to rebuild the coordination table using the independent channel Gamma-9 as the authoritative measurement source.
